title: A Sharp Phase Transition, Finally Proved
hook: Add links to a network one by one and, past a critical density, a giant cluster snaps into existence. Mathematicians have now proved that jump is genuinely abrupt for a broad class of networks.
key_points: Percolation asks: if each link in a network exists with probability p, when does a giant connected cluster appear?
Below a critical p the clusters stay small; above it, one cluster spans the whole system.
Physicists long assumed that switch is sharp rather than gradual — a true phase transition.
Quanta reports mathematicians have now proved the abrupt change for a wide family of networks.
Percolation is the toy model for phase transitions generally, from freezing water to magnetization.
content_html: Take a big network and switch each possible link on with probability p. When p is small you get a scatter of little disconnected islands. Turn p up and, at some critical value, a single cluster suddenly spans the entire system. Physicists have long taken it for granted that this switch is a genuine, abrupt phase transition — not a gradual slide — but proving it for general networks resisted decades of effort.
extra_html: Quanta Magazine reports that mathematicians have now settled the question for a broad class of networks, showing the shift really does happen sharply at a critical point. That matters well beyond graph theory: percolation is the standard minimal model for collective change of every kind — water freezing, a magnet aligning, a forest fire spreading — because it reduces a phase transition to one tunable knob and one critical value. A proof of sharpness in the general case puts the physicists' long-standing intuition on firm mathematical ground. Leila Sloman's write-up covers the proof and its history.

related.title: States of Matter
related.hook: Solid, liquid, gas, plasma — the difference is how tightly particles are bound. Add heat and matter changes state, but during the change the temperature holds still.

related.title: Entropy & the Arrow of Time
related.hook: Why does a smashed cup never reassemble itself? The second law of thermodynamics says disorder almost always wins.

related.title: Entropy Is Only Half the Arrow of Time
related.hook: Entropy production tells you which way time points. A second quantity — frenesy, the sheer busyness of a driven system — is what decides which structures survive.

flashcards.prompt: What is percolation, in one sentence?
flashcards.back_html: A model where each link in a network is present with probability p, used to ask when the small scattered clusters suddenly merge into one giant cluster spanning the whole system.

flashcards.prompt: Why do physicists care about percolation beyond networks?

choices.text: It is the simplest model of a phase transition, so lessons carry over to freezing, boiling and magnetization
It gives the exact melting temperature of any real material
It replaces thermodynamics for systems near absolute zero

flashcards.explanation_html: Percolation strips a phase transition down to its bare bones — a tunable parameter and a critical value — which is why it serves as the reference model for abrupt collective change.

flashcards.prompt: What does it mean for a phase transition to be 'sharp'?
flashcards.back_html: The system's behaviour changes discontinuously at a single critical value of the control parameter, rather than drifting smoothly from one regime to the other.
